title: Alone in Antarctica: 224 Days
logline: You're the winter caretaker of a remote Antarctic research station. Then the radio dies and footprints matching your boots start appearing in the snow.

thumbnail.scene: Split image. Left: the stick figure in the orange cap presses against a heavy door inside a dark room, holding an ice axe, eyes wide. Right: outside in the dark snow, a shadowy second figure in an orange cap raises a fist to knock. A trail of footprints leads to the door. Black and icy blue background with a bright red DAY 200.

locations.description: small insulated room: bunk bed, table with a radio and microphone, small heater, metal shelves of cans, wall covered in marker notes, one hanging bulb, heavy outer door
cramped room with a big boxy diesel generator, a round fuel gauge, a frosted fuel pipe, fuel cans on the floor
flat snowfield around a low red station building with a radio dish on the roof, a big round fuel tank and a vent pipe on the wall
flat snow runway lined with orange barrels, open sky above
dark flat ice with thin flags on poles every fifty meters, footprints along the trail
abandoned blue hut half buried in snow, 4920 painted above the door; inside: bunk, wooden desk with an old radio and a logbook, six fuel drums along the wall

beats.narration: Day 200. The generator just died.
beats.scene: The character sits up in a bunk in a dark room, lit only by a headlamp beam. The ceiling bulb is off.

beats.narration: It is minus fifty outside, and the heater is already ticking as it cools.
beats.scene: The character hugs their knees on the bunk, breath visible as a white puff, staring at a small heater.

beats.narration: Then you hear it. Three slow knocks on the outer door.
beats.scene: A heavy insulated door at the end of the room shudders. The character in the foreground freezes.
beats.animate_prompt: The door shakes three times as if knocked from outside

beats.narration: You are the only person for two thousand kilometers.
beats.scene: A tiny red station building alone in an endless dark field of snow under stars.

beats.narration: Nobody has walked across this ice in six months.
beats.scene: Smooth untouched snow stretching to the horizon, the station small in the distance.

beats.narration: To understand who is knocking, you have to go back to the day the last plane left.
beats.scene: The character stands by orange barrels on a snowy runway in daylight, looking up at the sky.

beats.narration: Day 1. The last supply plane of the season roars down the snow runway.
beats.scene: A small propeller plane lifts off the white runway. The character waves from beside an orange barrel.
beats.animate_prompt: The plane takes off and climbs out of frame

beats.narration: Your job is simple. Keep this little research station running through the long Antarctic winter.
beats.scene: The character stands proudly in front of a low red building with a radio dish on its roof.

beats.narration: The scientists left with the plane. They come back when the sun does, about eight months from now.
beats.scene: The plane is a tiny dot in the sky. The character is alone on the empty runway.

beats.narration: Inside, you count everything. Two hundred and forty days of food, stacked in neat boxes.
beats.scene: The character holds a clipboard in front of tall metal shelves full of cans and boxes.

beats.narration: The tank outside holds enough diesel for the whole winter, if you are careful.
beats.scene: The character taps a big round fuel tank beside the station with a gloved hand.

beats.narration: There is one rule. Every Sunday at noon, you call the main base on the radio.
beats.scene: A radio sits on the table with a big calendar on the wall above it, Sundays circled.

beats.narration: Day 7. Your first Sunday. You press the button and say your station name.
beats.scene: The character sits at the table holding a radio microphone to their mouth.

beats.narration: A friendly voice answers right away. Copy you loud and clear. How's the quiet?
beats.scene: The radio speaker glows with sound lines coming out of it. The character grins.

beats.narration: You laugh and say you love it. You almost mean it.
beats.scene: The character leans back in the chair laughing, the empty room behind them.

beats.narration: Day 14. The second call goes just as smoothly.
beats.scene: The character gives a thumbs up to the radio. A calendar shows two circled days crossed off.

beats.narration: Day 21. You press the button at noon. Static.
beats.scene: The character holds the microphone, frowning, as jagged static lines come from the speaker.

beats.narration: You try again at one o'clock. Then at two. Then at three.
beats.scene: A wall clock showing three. The character still holds the microphone, slumped forward.

beats.narration: The main base has never missed a call. Not once in forty years.
beats.scene: The character stares at the silent radio, microphone dangling from their hand.

beats.narration: Day 22. You take the radio apart on the table, piece by piece.
beats.scene: Radio parts spread across the table. The character holds a screwdriver and a small circuit board.

beats.narration: Every part looks fine. The power light glows green. The problem is not on your end.
beats.scene: Close on the radio with a small green light glowing. The character's hand hovers over it.

beats.narration: You try the satellite phone. It finds no signal, just one blinking bar.
beats.scene: The character holds a chunky satellite phone up toward the ceiling, squinting at its screen.

beats.narration: You climb onto the roof to check the dish. It is clean, and pointed right where it should be.
beats.scene: The character stands on the red station roof beside the radio dish, holding a flashlight.

beats.narration: So you do the math. If nobody is coming early, everything has to last.
beats.scene: The character writes numbers on a sheet of paper next to a stack of cans.

beats.narration: You cut your meals from three a day to two and a half. You write the plan on the wall.
beats.scene: The character writes a ration chart in marker on the wall beside the shelves.

beats.narration: You shut down two of the four rooms. Less space to heat means less fuel burned.
beats.scene: The character closes a door and tapes a sign on it reading CLOSED.

beats.narration: Day 40. You stand outside and watch the sun touch the horizon.
beats.scene: The character stands in the snow facing a low orange sun sitting on the horizon line.

beats.narration: It slides along the edge for an hour, then sinks. It will not rise again for four months.
beats.scene: Only a thin orange glow remains on the horizon. The character's shadow is long and faint.

beats.narration: Polar night has begun.
beats.scene: Total darkness with stars. The station window is the only small square of light.

beats.narration: That evening the radio, silent for weeks, crackles to life on its own.
beats.scene: The character spins around at the table, spoon in hand, as the radio light flickers.

beats.narration: A flat voice reads numbers. Four. Nine. Two. Zero. Then the static swallows it.
beats.scene: Close on the radio speaker with the numbers 4 9 2 0 floating out of it like sound waves.

beats.narration: You grab the microphone and shout your station name. Nobody answers.
beats.scene: The character yells into the microphone, leaning over the table.

beats.narration: You write the numbers on the wall. Four, nine, two, zero.
beats.scene: The character writes 4920 in big marker numbers on the wall next to the ration chart.

beats.narration: You don't know it yet, but those numbers are a warning.
beats.scene: The numbers 4920 on the wall, lit by a single swinging bulb.

beats.narration: Day 52. You wake up with a headache that will not go away.
beats.scene: The character sits on the edge of the bunk holding their head with both hands.

beats.narration: You feel dizzy when you stand. The bulb above you seems to swim.
beats.scene: The character wobbles in the middle of the room. The ceiling bulb is drawn doubled and blurry.

beats.narration: You know these signs from training. Carbon monoxide. The heater's exhaust has nowhere to go.
beats.scene: The character stares at the heater. A faint gray haze hangs near the ceiling.

beats.narration: You check the wall vent. Snow has packed the outside pipe solid.
beats.scene: A metal vent pipe sticking out of the station wall, completely plugged with hard snow.

beats.narration: You have maybe an hour before you pass out, and don't wake up.
beats.scene: A wall clock. The character leans against the wall, eyes half closed.

beats.narration: You shut the heater off and pull on every layer you own.
beats.scene: The character switches off the heater while stuffed into a huge puffy coat, hat and goggles.

beats.narration: Outside, a storm is screaming at a hundred kilometers an hour.
beats.scene: Sideways streaks of snow blur everything. The station is barely visible.

beats.narration: You clip a rope from your belt to the door handle. In a whiteout, people die three meters from home.
beats.scene: The character clips a rope from their waist to the station door handle, snow blasting past.

beats.narration: You crawl along the wall, one glove on the building at all times.
beats.scene: The character crawls on hands and knees along the station wall, the rope trailing behind.

beats.narration: The vent pipe is buried under a hard drift. You hack at it with an ice axe.
beats.scene: The character swings a small ice axe at a snow drift covering the vent pipe.

beats.narration: Ten minutes. Twenty. Your fingers stop feeling like fingers.
beats.scene: The character's gloved hand is frozen in a claw shape around the axe handle, frost on the glove.

beats.narration: Finally the pipe breaks free, and a puff of gray air bursts out.
beats.scene: The vent pipe is clear and a cloud of gray smoke shoots out. The character falls back in the snow.
beats.animate_prompt: A gray puff of smoke blasts out of the vent pipe and the character falls backward

beats.narration: Back inside, you sit by the cracked-open door, gulping clean air.
beats.scene: The character slumps against the wall by the open door, breathing hard, snow drifting in.

beats.narration: You make a new rule. Check the vent every morning, no matter what.
beats.scene: The character writes CHECK VENT EVERY MORNING on the wall in big letters.

beats.narration: Day 53. The storm is gone. You step outside to check the vent, like you promised.
beats.scene: Calm, starry night. The character walks out of the station door holding a flashlight.

beats.narration: In the fresh snow, there are footprints.
beats.scene: A flashlight beam lights up a line of deep boot prints in smooth snow.

beats.narration: They start at the radio dish and stop right at your door.
beats.scene: Top-down view: a trail of footprints from the base of the radio dish to the station door, where the character stands.

beats.narration: You stand very still. Your flashlight is shaking.
beats.scene: The character stands frozen, flashlight beam trembling across the snow.

beats.narration: They are boot prints. Big ones, with heavy treads, like yours.
beats.scene: A single boot print in the snow with a deep zigzag tread pattern.

beats.narration: You put your own boot beside one. They match perfectly.
beats.scene: The character's boot is placed right next to a print. Same size and same tread.

beats.narration: You tell yourself you made them yesterday, during the storm.
beats.scene: The character looks back over their shoulder at the station, forcing a nervous smile.

beats.narration: But you never went near the dish. And the storm would have erased anything older than an hour.
beats.scene: The radio dish on its pole, with the footprints starting right under it.

beats.narration: Back inside, you lock the door. Then you shove a shelf of cans in front of it.
beats.scene: The character pushes a heavy metal shelf of cans against the door. A few cans fall.
beats.animate_prompt: The character shoves the shelf across the floor and cans tumble off the top

beats.narration: That night you don't sleep. You sit facing the door, the ice axe across your knees.
beats.scene: The character sits in a chair facing the blocked door, ice axe on their lap, eyes wide.

beats.narration: Nothing happens. No sound but the wind.
beats.scene: The same scene later. The character's head is nodding, the door unmoved.

beats.narration: Day 60. More footprints. This time they lead away from the station, across the ice.
beats.scene: Footprints head away from the station door into dark open snow.

beats.narration: You follow them a few hundred meters with your flashlight, then stop.
beats.scene: The character stands on dark flat ice, flashlight pointing along footprints that continue into blackness.

beats.narration: They head toward the old station. An abandoned hut two kilometers away, closed since the nineteen nineties.
beats.scene: Far in the distance, a faint outline of a small hut. A row of old flags leads toward it.

beats.narration: You turn back. Nobody has been inside that hut in thirty years.
beats.scene: The character walks back toward the station, glancing over their shoulder at the dark.

beats.narration: Day 90. The generator coughs twice, and every light goes out.
beats.scene: The ceiling bulb goes dark mid-flicker. The character looks up from a can of beans.
beats.animate_prompt: The bulb flickers twice and goes out, leaving the room black

beats.narration: In total darkness, the station starts to cool right away.
beats.scene: A black room. Only the character's white breath and the outline of their face are visible.

beats.narration: You find your headlamp by touch and head to the generator room.
beats.scene: The character enters a small room with a big diesel generator, headlamp beam on.

beats.narration: The fuel gauge reads almost half. That's not the problem.
beats.scene: Close on a round fuel gauge with the needle just under half.

beats.narration: You touch the fuel line. It's frozen. At minus sixty, diesel turns into thick gel.
beats.scene: The character grips a pipe running into the generator. The pipe is coated in frost.

beats.narration: You wrap the pipe in rags and hold your camp stove under it, carefully, a hand's width away.
beats.scene: The character crouches, holding a small camp stove with a blue flame under a rag-wrapped pipe.

beats.narration: One mistake, and the whole room goes up in flames.
beats.scene: Close on the small blue flame near a dripping pipe, a fuel can nearby.

beats.narration: After two hours, the gel starts to flow. You pull the cord. The generator roars back.
beats.scene: The character yanks the starter cord. The generator shakes to life with puffs of exhaust.
beats.animate_prompt: The character pulls the cord and the generator rumbles to life, shaking

beats.narration: But then you check the tank outside, and your stomach drops.
beats.scene: The character stands by the big fuel tank, flashlight aimed at the ground.

beats.narration: The frozen line hid a slow leak. A dark stain spreads across the snow under the tank.
beats.scene: A big dark puddle shape in the snow under the fuel tank, with a dripping valve.

beats.narration: You've lost almost a third of your diesel. Not enough to reach spring.
beats.scene: The character crosses out numbers on the ration chart on the wall and writes a smaller one.

beats.narration: Day 95. You move your bed into the generator room. It's the only warm spot left.
beats.scene: A mattress on the floor beside the generator. The character lies wrapped in blankets.

beats.narration: You eat cold food to save fuel. Every morning you take a vitamin C tablet, so your gums don't bleed.
beats.scene: The character sits on the mattress holding a small pill and an open cold can.

beats.narration: You talk out loud to keep yourself company. You tell jokes to the cans.
beats.scene: The character holds up a can and talks to it, smiling weakly. A row of cans sits like an audience.

beats.narration: Then you remember the old station. Abandoned stations sometimes leave fuel drums behind.
beats.scene: The character sits up straight with a sudden idea, a lightbulb drawn over their head.

beats.narration: It's two kilometers in the dark, on the same trail as the footprints.
beats.scene: The dark trail of flags, the faded footprints running alongside them.

beats.narration: Day 110. You load a sled, check your rope, and step out onto the ice.
beats.scene: The character, bundled up, pulls an empty sled out onto the dark ice, headlamp on.

beats.narration: Flags mark the old trail every fifty meters. You walk from one to the next.
beats.scene: The character walks past a thin flag on a pole. Another flag is faint in the distance.

beats.narration: The cold burns your lungs. Your eyelashes freeze. You count your steps to stay calm.
beats.scene: Close on the character's goggles caked with frost, breath freezing in the air.

beats.narration: After an hour, a shape rises out of the dark. A blue hut, half buried in snow.
beats.scene: A small blue hut sticking out of a snow drift, lit by the character's headlamp.

beats.narration: The door is not buried. Someone has dug it out. Faded numbers are painted above it. Four, nine, two, zero.
beats.scene: A cleared doorway in the snow. Above the door, faded paint reads 4920.

beats.narration: Inside, the air is still. Your headlamp finds six fuel drums along the wall. Full.
beats.scene: A dusty room with six metal drums lined up against the wall.

beats.narration: You almost cry. That's enough to last until spring.
beats.scene: The character hugs one of the drums, eyes closed.

beats.narration: Then your light lands on the bunk in the corner.
beats.scene: A headlamp beam lands on a narrow bunk bed in the corner of the hut.

beats.narration: The blanket is folded neatly. There is a dent in the pillow.
beats.scene: A neatly folded blanket and a pillow with a head-shaped dent.

beats.narration: On the desk sits an old radio. Its dial is turned to your frequency.
beats.scene: An old radio on a wooden desk, its dial needle on a mark labeled with the character's station name.

beats.narration: Beside it is a logbook. The last entry should be thirty years old.
beats.scene: The character opens a thick leather logbook on the desk.

beats.narration: But the pages keep going, in fresh ink.
beats.scene: Close on logbook pages filled with fresh dark handwriting.

beats.narration: Day 22, radio dead, cut meals. Day 52, vent blocked. Day 90, fuel line froze.
beats.scene: The character's finger traces entries in the logbook. The headlamp shakes slightly.

beats.narration: Every entry is something that happened to you. In handwriting that looks just like yours.
beats.scene: The character holds the logbook next to their own notepad. The handwriting matches.

beats.narration: You flip to the last written page. It holds only one line.
beats.scene: The character turns a page slowly. The rest of the book is blank.

beats.narration: Day 200. I knock.
beats.scene: Close on the page: one line reading DAY 200. I KNOCK.

beats.narration: You drag two drums back that night. Then two more, each week after.
beats.scene: The character leans forward hauling a sled with two fuel drums across the dark ice.

beats.narration: Your shoulders ache. Your hands crack in the cold. But the generator keeps running.
beats.scene: The character rolls a drum into the generator room. The generator hums.

beats.narration: You never touch the logbook again. You leave it on the desk, exactly where it was.
beats.scene: The closed logbook alone on the desk in the empty hut.

beats.narration: But every night, you stare at the numbers on your wall. Four, nine, two, zero.
beats.scene: The character lies in the bunk, staring at 4920 written on the wall.

beats.narration: Day 199. Tomorrow is the day in the logbook.
beats.scene: A wall calendar with 199 crossed off and 200 circled in red.

beats.narration: You fill the generator with fresh fuel, just to be sure.
beats.scene: The character pours diesel from a can into the generator's tank.

beats.narration: You check the vent. You check the fuel line. Everything is fine.
beats.scene: The character runs a gloved hand along the clear, unfrozen fuel line, nodding.

beats.narration: You lie awake, listening.
beats.scene: The character lies in the bunk, eyes wide open in the dim room.

beats.narration: Day 200. At three in the morning, the generator coughs. Then it dies.
beats.scene: The room goes dark. The character bolts upright in the bunk.

beats.narration: The fuel line is clear. The tank is full. There is no reason for it to stop.
beats.scene: The character shines a headlamp on the silent generator. The gauge reads full.

beats.narration: The room goes quiet. The heater ticks as it cools.
beats.scene: The character stands in the dark, breath puffing, the small heater beside them.

beats.narration: Then come three slow knocks on the outer door.
beats.scene: The heavy door shudders. The character in the foreground grips the ice axe.
beats.animate_prompt: The door shakes three times as if knocked from outside

beats.narration: You don't breathe. You grip the ice axe with both hands.
beats.scene: Close on the character's hands squeezing the ice axe handle.

beats.narration: A voice comes through the door, flat and calm. It's your voice.
beats.scene: The character presses against the wall beside the door, eyes squeezed shut.

beats.narration: Don't open it yet, it says. Not until the sun comes back.
beats.scene: Close on the door with faint sound lines coming through the gap underneath.

beats.narration: Footsteps crunch away across the snow. Then nothing.
beats.scene: Fresh footprints lead away from the station door into darkness. No one is visible.

beats.narration: You sit against the door until morning. You never open it.
beats.scene: The character sits on the floor with their back against the door, axe in their lap.

beats.narration: Day 212. A thin orange line glows on the horizon.
beats.scene: The character stands outside watching a faint orange stripe on a dark horizon.

beats.narration: Day 220. The sun rises for the first time in four months. You let it hit your face.
beats.scene: Sunlight on the snow. The character stands with arms wide and eyes closed.

beats.narration: Day 224. A low buzz in the sky. A plane, the first in seven months.
beats.scene: The character looks up at a small plane in a bright blue sky.

beats.narration: It lands on the snow runway. You run toward it, waving both arms.
beats.scene: The plane touches down in a spray of snow while the character runs at it, waving.
beats.animate_prompt: The plane lands and slides to a stop as the character runs toward it, arms waving

beats.narration: The pilot climbs down and stares at you. She does not smile.
beats.scene: A stick-figure pilot in a flight helmet stands by the plane door, staring at the character.

beats.narration: Who are you, she asks. The caretaker of this station flew out with us. Seven months ago.
beats.scene: The pilot points at the character. The character takes a step back.

beats.narration: Behind her, someone else steps out of the plane. He is wearing an orange cap.
beats.scene: A second stick figure in an identical orange cap steps out of the plane door.

beats.narration: He looks right at you and says, see? I told you not to open the door.
beats.scene: The second orange-cap figure faces the character across the runway. They look exactly alike.
